A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRISM and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The retained material can be matched reliably despite pagination changes and appendix-table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original cross-domain detection experiments on True-False and LogicStruct, prompt and layer ablations, and internal-state analyses, including Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds TruthfulQA experiments, EUBHD baseline results, and a correlation analysis.

M1.justification: PRISM retains the same prompt generation, variance-ratio selection, feature extraction, and integration with MM and SAPLMA. Section 4 clarifies the existing training procedure without changing it; TruthfulQA uses the existing Prompt 3.

E1.justification: Section 5.5.4 adds TruthfulQA, described as 790 questions across 37 categories, with generated answers evaluated for hallucination. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained True-False and LogicStruct statement-classification tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds EUBHD to the existing True-False and LogicStruct comparisons in Tables 3–5 and evaluates SelfCheckGPT alongside MM and SAPLMA on TruthfulQA in Table 8. These additions broaden the evaluated alternatives to focused uncertainty estimation and multiple-response consistency; the previous comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new TruthfulQA evaluation introduces greedy answer generation, BLEURT-based labels at thresholds 0, 0.25, and 0.5, an ordered first-20% training/remaining-80% testing split, and AUROC. SelfCheckGPT uses 20 additional samples at temperature 1 with GPT-4 consistency assessment. These are new protocols; the existing benchmark protocols remain.

E4.justification: Section 5.5.1 adds a Pearson analysis relating the existing variance ratios to prompt accuracies. Table 8 additionally evaluates sensitivity to three BLEURT labeling thresholds. The previous prompt, layer, internal-state, and Appendix B analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces a Pearson significance test, reporting r=0.7708 and p=0.0055 in Section 5.5.1. Three-seed averaging was already reported in v2 and is also used for TruthfulQA; no increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged, but Tables 3–5 gain EUBHD scores and Table 8 adds TruthfulQA AUROCs for five methods at three thresholds. At BLEURT threshold 0.5, PRISM-SAPLMA scores 0.7248, SAPLMA 0.6654, and SelfCheckGPT 0.6357. These extend the result coverage rather than demonstrate a performance change between versions under an existing setting.

T1.justification: The truthfulness-direction, covariance, variance-ratio, and cosine-similarity mathematics in Equations (1)–(7) is unchanged. New Equation (8) merely states the standard formula for the accuracy metric already used; no substantive theoretical development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about prompt-guided internal states improving cross-domain hallucination detection. The additional experiments support those claims without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.5.4 newly interprets TruthfulQA results as evidence of effectiveness in more complex, real-world hallucination scenarios and explains the ordered split as testing cross-domain generalization. Existing mechanism explanations and the limitations discussion are unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies that LN-PP thresholds are optimized on training data, which clarifies an existing experiment rather than establishes a setting change. It also documents generation, labeling, sampling, and training details for TruthfulQA. Existing detector specifications, appendix templates, and code/data access information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to TruthfulQA by Lin et al. (2022) and representation engineering by Zou et al. (2023), plus a short statement about prior evidence for internal truthfulness representations. Previously cited uncertainty and consistency methods receive additional comparator discussion; the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in Sections 3–4, an explanation of accuracy, reordered baseline descriptions, and the new Section 5.5.4. Author/contact formatting changes, and Limitations and Ethics Statement become unnumbered. The main narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 8, expands Tables 3–5 with EUBHD rows, and relocates Table 7 through text reflow. Appendix Tables 8–10 become Tables 9–11 without substantive display changes. Figures 1–3 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical relevance by evaluating generated answers on TruthfulQA and adding relevant comparators while preserving v2's evidence. The gain is limited by the single-model, BLEURT-labeled new evaluation. The added prompt-selection statistic also needs qualification: r=0.7708 matches inclusion of the 'Without' entry in Tables 2 and 6; the ten prompts alone give approximately 0.557 from the printed values.
